reason: The passage explicitly demonstrates agency exercised by non-leaders. The text shows individual Israelite men and women independently requesting vessels of silver and gold from their Egyptian neighbors (וְיִשְׁאֲלוּ אִישׁ מֵאֵת רֵעֵהוּ וְאִשָּׁה מֵאֵת רְעוּתָהּ). The Israelite people collectively take action by lifting their dough and departing (וַיִּשָּׂא הָעָם אֶת־ בְּצֵקוֹ). Even ordinary Egyptians demonstrate agency as they are strengthened to hasten the people's departure (וַתֶּחֱזַק מִצְרַיִם עַל־ הָעָם). While leaders like Moses, Pharaoh, and God certainly exercise agency, the passage clearly attributes significant actions to common individuals and populations beyond leadership circles.
